title: Reflection and Rotation on the Coordinate Plane

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how images in a mirror are formed? This is similar to how reflection works in geometry!

blocks.markdown: In geometry, transformations help us to move or change shapes in a plane. Two common transformations are reflection and rotation. Reflection creates a mirror image of a shape, while rotation turns a shape around a fixed point.

blocks.title: Reflection
blocks.text: Reflection is a transformation that flips a figure over a line, creating a mirror image. Common lines of reflection include the x-axis, y-axis, and the line $y = x$.

blocks.markdown: When reflecting a point $(x, y)$ in the x-axis, the image is $(x, -y)$. Reflecting in the y-axis gives $(-x, y)$, and reflecting in the line $y = x$ results in $(y, x)$. Let's see how this works with an example.

blocks.title: Reflecting a Point
blocks.prompt: Reflect the point $(3, 4)$ in the x-axis.

steps.text: Identify the coordinates of the point: $(3, 4)$.
To reflect in the x-axis, change the sign of the y-coordinate: $(3, -4)$.

blocks.markdown: Rotation involves turning a point or shape around a fixed point, often the origin. A 90° rotation counterclockwise about the origin transforms $(x, y)$ to $(-y, x)$. A 180° rotation changes $(x, y)$ to $(-x, -y)$.

blocks.title: Rotation
blocks.text: When rotating 90° counterclockwise, swap the coordinates and change the sign of the new x-coordinate. For 180°, change the signs of both coordinates.

points: Reflection flips a point or shape over a line, resulting in a mirror image.
Rotation turns a point or shape around a fixed point, such as the origin.
